quote: Oh, my neighbors have it, and I had some guy come from Sunrun who gave me a quote.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a competitor (Sunrun) already gave a quote. The rep asks one light qualifying follow-up ('are you just looking to find the best quote, or what is it that you're looking for in a company?') but never probes what Sunrun actually quoted, what the terms were, or why the customer is shopping further — competitive intel that would help the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that pricing/terms probing is closer-tier content and deliberately stayed shallow to avoid scope creep.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one more layer deep on competitor mentions — 'what did Sunrun show you for prices/panels?' — without engaging in a pricing debate. This is free intel for the closer.

quote: Oh, yeah. I got that. But this guy told me that from Sunrise, there was gonna spent a great big beautiful bill next to them.
stewart_read: Customer raises a tax-credit/legislation-based skepticism trigger tied to a prior competitor conversation. Rep responds with a factual patch ('we've been able to get a lot of new incentives in place of that') rather than flipping the objection back toward the customer's bill pain.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive handling — the rep treated this as a factual question needing a factual answer rather than recognizing the emotional/skeptical undertone.
coaching_implication: When customers raise policy uncertainty, redirect to the concrete bill pain rather than defending federal policy changes in the weeds.

quote: I think that 28 panels might I think 28 panels for for us is high water wattage panels.
stewart_read: This is unprompted comparative panel-wattage explanation — the rep is doing the closer's job of justifying equipment specs. This is a heavier scope-creep instance than the earlier one-line battery confirmation, since it involves the rep constructing a technical comparison rather than answering a direct yes/no.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to drill in the 1-on-1: redirect with 'the specialist will walk you through exact panel counts and wattage once we have your usage data' instead of freelancing a comparison.

quote: Yeah. We have batteries as well.
stewart_read: A brief, factual one-line confirmation that Ion offers batteries in response to a direct customer question. This is a much lower-severity instance than the 06:23 wattage comparison — it's a factual yes/no, not an unprompted technical justification — but it's still an opening the rep could bridge to the specialist rather than confirm outright.
alternative_hypothesis: This may be an acceptable minimal answer since the customer asked directly and a flat denial would kill rapport; scope creep concerns apply more to volunteered explanation than to short factual confirmations.
coaching_implication: Low-priority coaching note — this one-liner is closer to acceptable direct-answer territory than a genuine scope violation; don't conflate it with the heavier 06:23 instance in feedback.

quote: My mom passed away. We're having a funeral on
stewart_read: Customer discloses a significant loss. Rep responds at 11:28 with 'Okay. After the second. Alright. I'm sorry to hear that, by the way,' which does meet the schema's specific-acknowledgment bar, then immediately pivots to scheduling logic. This is adequate-but-thin rather than a genuine miss — the acknowledgment is real, just brief.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would call this a miss outright, but the transcript shows a specific, personalized acknowledgment ('I'm sorry to hear that, by the way') rather than silence or a generic platitude, so full 'miss' classification overstates the gap.
coaching_implication: Coach for depth, not absence: a half-beat pause before returning to logistics would let the acknowledgment land instead of being immediately buried by 'but do the fourth or the fifth.'

quote: I'll send you a text with the appointment details so you can add it to your calendar. But other than that, that's everything I have for you today.
stewart_read: The button-up only completes the datetime and text-followup promise. The one-hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, and 'is that fair?' handshake are all skipped, and the co-owner (wife, identified at 01:47) is never invited onto the call. Combined, this appointment carries real no-show and fragile-attendance risk despite having a locked day and time.
coaching_implication: Walk the rep through the full button-up checklist on this call specifically — the gap is not just missing phrasing, it compounds with an unconfirmed co-owner into a genuinely fragile booking the closer may show up to without the decision-maker present.
